exclude: screen matrix and sprite pointers (VIC bank 0)
upper half of the character set: load_stage_charset copies the stage's own set here at each stage start (at the hand-over, stage 6's)
the stage's event list, copied here from the stage's block by load_stage_block at each stage start

comments.text: The processor port and the bytes after it, as the snapshot holds them. title_charset and start_stage_run clear bit 1 of $01 to switch the BASIC and KERNAL ROMs out, so the stage data under them at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF can be read.
The processor port, whose bit 1 title_charset and start_stage_run clear to switch the ROMs out.
X kept by shots_vs_blocks while it rubs out a block.
A working byte of move_hatch while it picks the opening shape.
cell_x kept by irq_chain over the interrupt's work, put back by irq_exit.
cell_y kept by irq_chain, put back by irq_exit.
Low byte of the screen pointer that screen_addr sets; many routines borrow $FB/$FC for other addresses.
High byte of the screen pointer.
Low byte of a second pointer: the map in map_column, the colour RAM cell in the laser code.
High byte of the second pointer.
The colour bar_highlight paints the lit box of the power-up bar in this frame.
The scores of up to five players, ten digits each; the one playing is copied into score_digits at the start of a turn.
Lives left of each of the five players: 3 at the start.
The stage each of the five players has reached, put back at the start of their turn.
Each player's music setting (music_on), kept between turns.
Low byte of the IRQ vector.
High byte of the IRQ vector, which irq_off points back at the KERNAL's $EA31.

A BASIC line left at the start of the program: 9 SYS 5768, which would start the game at $1688. Nothing runs it, as the loader and the unpackers jump to $1688 themselves. The bytes after it are the remains of other BASIC lines from the developer's disk: "C)LM87 SIM. P." and "NO RASTER FLICKER !!!", cut off where the NMI code begins.

The NMI handler. CIA 2's timers A and B, started at fixed raster lines by start_split_timers, interrupt twice a frame: timer A puts the playfield's fine scroll (scroll_x) and multicolour into $D016 and turns extended colour off; timer B turns extended colour on with no scroll for the power-up bar. Saves only A.
Leftover bytes from the developer's disk: the remains of a BASIC line (WAIT 24439, ...) and some code, never run.
Tests sprite collisions (check_collisions), then reads the keyboard for pause: with P down it enters pause, otherwise it updates the power-up bar.
Leftover bytes that nothing runs: remains of BASIC lines and an older character-copying loop.
The aimed balls (balls_frame) and the aimed bullets.
Leftover bytes that nothing reads: the PETSCII text 6CHAR3",8, apparently from the developer's disk commands.
Sets all three voices' pitch from the first sprite's height, then plays a sound and moves on. Called while the ship explodes.
Leftover bytes, the end of the same text.
Steps the sound effects (effects_tick), then the movers.
Leftover bytes that nothing runs: two JMP $7623 and the start of another instruction.

Pause, entered with interrupts off: keeps the screen split by watching the raster (line 74 for the playfield, 228 for the bar) and keeps the music and the bar going, until P is pressed again; then waits for P to be let go.
Jumps to play_frame_tail.
If P is down, turns the raster interrupt off, waits for P to be let go, runs pause_loop, and turns the interrupt back on.
Leftover bytes after the RTS: the tail of a delay loop and a CLI, never run.
Lights the power-up bar's current choice: resets the six boxes to colour 11, then paints the five cells of the chosen box in a colour from bar_flash, which cycles each call.
Eight colours the chosen power-up box cycles through.
Counter that steps through bar_flash.
Paints the six power-up boxes colour 11 and loads X with the current choice (powerup_pos).
Aimed balls, six slots: X low byte, worked as a pixel position.
Each ball's X high byte.
Frames left in each ball's current growth step; starts random, 1 to 20.
The fraction of X, carried between frames, so a ball can move at less than a pixel a frame.
The fraction of Y.
Their Y; 0 when the slot is free.
The sprite slot each ball rides.
Whole pixels a frame each ball moves sideways.
1 when the ball moves right, 0 when it moves left.
Whole pixels a frame each ball moves up or down.
1 when the ball moves down, 0 when it moves up.
The fraction of its vertical speed.
The fraction of its sideways speed.
Growth steps left before a new ball sets off: it shows shapes $C8 down to $C2 as it grows, one step every four frames.

Starts an aimed ball at the cell in cell_x and cell_y: takes a free sprite slot (1 to 6) and ball slot, multiplies the column by four into a pixel X, aims it at the Vic Viper (aim_ball), and shows it growing in place, grey, from shape $C8. A ball that would not move at all is cancelled.
Unused bytes.

Moves the six aimed balls: a growing ball counts its growth and, when grown, aims again at the ship and turns blue; a moving ball adds its speed and fraction each frame. One that leaves Y $4C-$C1 or the sides, or whose sprite has been switched off, is freed.

Aims ball X at the Vic Viper: the difference in Y and the difference in X (in two-pixel units) become the vertical and sideways speeds, scaled by four and eight, with whole and fractional parts, and their directions; so a ball always reaches the ship's position of the moment in the same number of frames.
A spare RTS after aim_ball.
Launches an aimed ball from a random point: column 5 to 70 and Y $50 to $C7.
Launches an aimed ball from column 65 at a height that steps down 20 pixels each call, from $64 round through $C7 back to $50.
The height ball_from_right uses next.
Code that nothing calls: a loop that waits for raster line 255 and runs the volcano's eruption and rocks (erupt, move_vrocks) and draw_sprites, a test of stage 4's volcano on its own.
44 steps of a sine wave, from 0 up to 30, down through 0 to -31 and back, that the swooping fliers add to their row.
The row the next swooping pair is centred on; random, $6E to $95.
Swooping fliers, six slots: X high byte.
Swooping fliers, X low byte.
Swooping fliers, the row their wave is centred on; 0 when free.
Swooping fliers, 1 while flying left, 0 once they turn back right.
Swooping fliers, where each is in swoop_wave.
Swooping fliers, the sprite slot each rides.
Swooping fliers, the shape each shows, $CE to $D2 in turn.

Starts a swooping flier at cell_x (and X high byte) and cell_y in a free sprite slot, shape $D8 and blue; every seventh one is red (colour 2), and leaves a capsule when shot. If no sprite slot is free, the spawning stops and a new centre row is chosen.
Fliers until the next red one.
Where in the wave a new flier starts: 0 or 22, so a pair fly in opposite phase.
Frames until the next pair.
Pairs still to come in this wave.
Set while this stage sends swooping fliers.
While swooping fliers are on, every ten frames sends a pair from the right edge at swoop_y, one at each phase of the wave; then moves them (move_swoopers).
Which three of the six fliers move this frame: 0 or 3.
Fliers left to move this frame.

Moves three of the six swooping fliers each frame: each steps along swoop_wave, animates every second step, and flies four pixels a frame left, turning back right at X $1C; one that leaves at the right is freed.
Character-drawn pieces, nine slots: X in two-pixel units (the column is half of it).
Each piece's first character; a piece is four characters, two by two.
Each piece's Y in quarter rows (the row is a quarter of it); 0 when free.
Cleared by stage_setup; nothing else uses it.
Each piece's vertical step: -1, 0 or 1.
Starts a piece at cell_x, cell_y with the direction in piece_new_dy and the characters in piece_new_char, in the first free slot.
The vertical step for the next piece.
Throws out three pieces from one point: one rising (characters $DC), one level ($D8) and one falling ($E0), as the big carrier opens.
Moves the pieces: each is erased, steps a half column left and one quarter row up or down, and is drawn again in colour 14; one that reaches the left edge or leaves the playfield's height is freed.
The first character for the next piece, and a counter while drawing it.
Frees the piece.
Frames until spawn_carriers sends the next big carrier.
Every 25 to 64 frames sends a big carrier from the right edge at a random height (spawn_carrier).
Big carriers, six slots: X low byte.
Each carrier's X high byte.
The fraction of X, so they can move at a pixel and a half a frame.
Their Y; 0 when free.
Hits each carrier can still take: 6.
Whole pixels a frame each moves left: 3, and 2 once it has opened.
A spare zero between carrier_speed and carrier_slot.
The sprite slot each rides.
Starts a big carrier at the right edge (X $1FF) at cell_y: a double-size blue sprite, shape $D3, six hits, moving left three and a half pixels a frame.

Moves the big carriers left (speed plus half a pixel). A shot switches the sprite off for a moment; each such hit takes one of its six, and it comes back until they run out. Once on the left half of the screen it slows to two, takes the open shape $D4 and throws out three pieces (split_pieces). One that leaves at the left is freed.
Low byte of each of the six darts' X.
High byte of each dart's X.
Each dart's Y; 0 when free.
Hits each dart can still take: 20 when it starts.
Which side of its rectangle each dart is flying: 0 down, 1 right, 2 up, 3 left.
The sprite slot each dart rides.
X of the four corners of the darts' circuit: $028, $028, $11E, $11E (high bytes at $1137).
High bytes of the corners' X.
Y of the corners: $7C, $B2, $B2, $7C. A dart that reaches corner n turns onto leg n.
Sideways step of each leg: 0 none, 2 right, 1 left (two pixels a frame).
Vertical step of each leg: 2 down, 0, -2 up, 0.

Moves the darts round their rectangle: in from the right along Y $7C, down the left side, right along the bottom and up the right side, cutting back left early once above the Vic Viper. A hit switches the sprite off; it comes back flashing, with one hit fewer, and when none are left it is destroyed. One that leaves at the left is freed. Shapes $D5-$D8 turn every fourth frame.
Frames left of each dart's flash after a hit; indexes dart_flash_colours.
The end of dart_flash: a spare zero.
Colours of a dart's flash, brown and white by turns (byte 0 its own colour, 9).
Frees a dart and its double-size sprite.
Brings a dart in at X $150, Y $7C, flying left: brown, shape $D5, twenty hits.
Frame counter for the darts' animation.
Darts still to be sent; stage 4's attack sets it to 6.
Every 60 frames, while darts_to_come is not 0, sends a dart.
Frames until the next dart.
Frame counter for the volcano's rocks.
Low byte of the volcano's X; it moves left with the scenery.
High byte of the volcano's X.
A spare byte after volcano_x_hi.
Low byte of each of the six volcano rocks' X.
High byte of each rock's X.
The sprite slot each rock rides.
Each rock's Y; 0 when free.
Each rock's sideways drift, 0 to 8, less the four pixels the scenery moves.
Each rock's vertical speed, 4 to 7 at first, lowered by one every fourth frame so it slows, stops and turns back.
Throws a rock from the volcano at Y $6C: a random speed down, a random drift, shape $AD-$AF and colour from vrock_colours.
Colours of the volcano's rocks: brown, dark grey and red.
Moves the volcano's rocks: each falls, slows and climbs again as its speed runs down, drifting with the scenery. One that leaves Y $50-$C7, or whose sprite was switched off by a hit, is freed.

Tests each double-size sprite (carriers, darts) against the player's shots and lasers: a shot within five cells is rubbed out and the sprite is switched to 2, the mark of a hit, which its own mover then counts.
First character of each of the four rows of a floor head's picture, top to bottom: $8C, $92, $98, $9E.
Characters left to draw on the head's row: 6.
Screen offsets of a head's four rows, top to bottom.
How far the head being drawn has come out, 0 to 3: rows of it that show, less one.

Draws a stage 5 head rising out of the floor at cell_x, cell_y: as many rows of its picture as head_step allows, the top of the head in the lowest of its four rows at first and moving up a row each step. Each row is six consecutive characters.
The screen row the head drawer is on.
The row of the head's picture being drawn.
Column of each of the four heads still coming out.
The second head's column, moved left by shift_objects.
The third head's column.
The fourth head's column.
Row of each.
0 for a head rising from the floor, 1 for one coming down from the ceiling.
How far each has come out, 0 to 3; 4 when done, $FF when the slot is free.
Starts a head coming out at cell_x, cell_y, of type head_type, and arms it (arm_head).
The type of the head being added.
Frames until the heads come out another row: every 12 frames.
Every 12 frames brings each head that is coming out a row further, drawing it the right way for its type, until all four rows show.
X kept by grow_heads.
The head has come right out: frees its slot in the rising list.
First character of each row of a ceiling head's picture: $AE, $B4, $BA, $C0.
Screen offsets of a ceiling head's rows, bottom to top.
Draws a head coming down from the ceiling: the same as draw_head_up with the rows in the other order.
Column of each of the six heads that can fire (head_fire).
Row of each; 0 when free.
Frames before each head first opens its mouth: 60.

Gives a new head a slot for firing: its position, a firing count of 60 (head_fire fires while the count is below 60, once every six calls), the row offset its rings leave from (head_rate_by_type) and ten hits.
Per type, the value arm_head puts in head_rate: 6 for floor heads, 8 for ceiling heads.
Hits each head can still take: 10.
Per head, how often it fires.
Set to 1 by title_keys when fire or RETURN is down; the attract loop starts a game on it.
How many passes in a row SPACE has been down on the title, stopping at 2; the attract loop steps the player count when it reaches 1.
Which player (0 to 3) game_loop is running.
Set to 1 by game_loop when the player it just ran still has lives, so the round of turns goes again.
Character codes of the logo's top row.
Character codes of the logo's bottom row.
Copies the two rows of the GRADIUS logo (17 characters each) to the screen at rows 6 and 7 in colour 9.

The game's first instruction, where the second unpacker hands over. Waits about 150 frames (wait_frames), turns the screen on (screen_on), clears the screen and sets up stage 0 (stage_setup), clears it again, sets two colours, turns every sprite off and copies the title's characters in (title_charset). Then the attract loop: draws the PLAYER GAME line and the title text, waits for raster line 255, moves the star field (title_stars) and reads the keys (title_keys). Fire or RETURN starts a game with the chosen number of players; SPACE, held for three passes, steps the count from one to four.
Number of players for the next game, 1 to 4, stepped by SPACE on the title (title_next_count) and shown by title_player_line.
Offset of each player's 10-digit score in score_store ($0200): 0, 10, 20, 30, 40.
Zeroes the 50 bytes at $0200-$0231 that hold five 10-digit scores, one per player slot.

One whole game. Gives every player three lives and the stage they last reached, then takes the players in turn: copies a player's score into the live score digits at $4000, sets the stage, runs the stage's play (stage_play, from $173A), and on return turns sprites and sound off. A player out of lives gets GAME OVER (game_over_text) and the high-score check; the others keep their score and stage. When nobody has lives left it reads RETURN once: held, a new game starts at once with three lives each; otherwise back to the title.
The words ONE, TWO, THREE and FOUR, eight ASCII bytes each, for the title and the PLAYER line.
Letters in each of ONE, TWO, THREE and FOUR.
" PLAYER GAME", ASCII padded with spaces, printed after the player count on the title.
Which of ONE to FOUR print_player_word prints (1 to 4).
Offset of that word in player_words.
Letters left to print.
Prints ONE, TWO, THREE or FOUR (word_number) at screen row 11 plus Y, in colour 9. Letters are ASCII, turned into screen codes by adding $40.
Prints the player count and " PLAYER GAME" on the title, row 11.
Steps player_count 1, 2, 3, 4, 1.
Reads the title's inputs: RETURN or fire on port 2 sets start_pressed; SPACE counts up space_held, which clears when it is let go.
The end of title_keys. This RTS stands where an LDA #$FF belongs: with $A9 here the routine runs on into cheat_key.

A cheat cut off by the RTS before it. With four players chosen, holding left SHIFT on the title sets cheat_mode and puts a "C" at the top-left of the screen. Restored, it works: play goes on through every hit.

Clears the screen and resets the stage (through $FE00), then prints "PLAYER " and the player's number word, as shown before each turn. Its third byte is followed by $FB $B0 $41, which the processor runs as ISC $41B0,Y (an undocumented instruction that adds one to a byte and subtracts it from A) where JSR $41B0 seems meant.
"GAME OVER" in ASCII.
Prints GAME OVER at the middle of the screen, in colour 9.
Waits for raster line 255 to come round 150 times, about three seconds on a PAL machine.
Loads the character set of stage 6 (index 5) into $3C00 (load_stage_charset) for the title, and puts the stage number back.
The stage each player starts on, copied to every player when a game begins.
Leftover bytes after start_stage that nothing runs: two loop tails with calls to $194A and $1953, and eight bytes of $FF.
Frequency table of the tune player: 63 notes as SID frequency words, from $0218 (about C-1) up a semitone at a time. A note byte plus the tune's transposition (tune_transpose) indexes it.
The frequency looked up for the note being started.
High byte of the frequency looked up for the note.
The byte just read from the voice's tune data: a note, or a command ($FE instrument, $FD jump, $FF restart).
Per voice, how much the pulse width (pulse_width) drops each tick.
Ticks left before the tune player steps again; reloaded from tune_tempo.
The tune player's instruments, 15 of them: waveform and gate byte of each. The $FE command picks one.
Attack and decay of each instrument.
Sustain and release of each instrument.
Pulse-width sweep of each instrument (pw_sweep).
Attack and decay of the instrument each of the two voices plays.
Sustain and release of the instrument each voice plays.
Per voice, tempo steps left in the note now sounding.
Per voice, low byte of where its tune data starts; set by set_tune, used by restart and jump commands.
Per voice, low byte of the next byte of tune data.
Per voice, high byte of where its tune data starts.
Per voice, high byte of the next byte of tune data.
The length byte read after a note, doubled; or the instrument number after an $FE.
Offset of each voice's registers in the SID: 0, 7 and 14.
Waveform byte of the instrument each voice plays.
Per voice, the pulse width's low byte: $F0 at each new note, then lowered by pw_sweep every tick.

The tune player, meant to run once a frame. Every tune_tempo frames it steps each voice: when its note runs out it reads the voice's data, two bytes a note (note, length); $FE sets the instrument, $FD jumps to the second section, $FF restarts both voices. A new note sets frequency, envelope and waveform and retriggers the gate; every tick lowers the pulse width. Nothing in the game calls it: its only callers are the test loop tune_test and music_tick, which nothing calls either, and it never ran in a code map of the title and all eight stages.
How many voices the tune player steps: 2.
The $FF command: puts both voices back at the start of their data, sets two voices and silences voice 3.

Clears the SID and sets the volume and the first two voices' envelopes to $09, then points both voices at the start of their data, each with one step left. Its loop stores from $D418 up 24 bytes, so it reaches the first two voices only through the SID's mirror at $D420 and never clears $D410-$D417 (voice 3's control and envelope, and the filter).
A test loop left in the game: starts tune 1 and plays it for ever, one tick a frame, flashing the border black and white to show how long each tick takes. Nothing calls it.
The $FE command: loads the instrument numbered note_length into the voice: waveform, envelope and pulse sweep.
The $FD command: moves the voice on to a fixed offset into its data (tune_jump_offset), turns voice 3 off and carries on reading.
Per voice, how far into its data the $FD command jumps: $62 and $10.
Frames between steps of the tune player: 6 for tune 1, 4 for tune 2.
Semitones added to every note: 12 for tune 1, 0 for tune 2.
Low bytes of tune 1's two voices ($1CA1 and $1D55).
High bytes of tune 1's two voices.
Low bytes of tune 2's two voices ($1DE9 and $1E9B).
High bytes of tune 2's two voices.

Chooses a tune: A = 1 picks tune 1 (tempo 6, an octave up), anything else tune 2 (tempo 4); then music_init. Two events call it as a stage starts (start_tune1, start_tune2), so the SID is cleared there, but the tune itself never plays (tune_tick).
Tune 1, first voice: pairs of note and length, with $FE instrument changes, ending $FD $FF.
Tune 1, second voice.
Tune 2, first voice.
Tune 2, second voice, a bass line of repeated octaves, ending $FF.
Six bytes after the last tune ($FF $00 $FD $00 $FD $00) that nothing reads.

Sprite shapes $80-$87, 64 bytes each from $2000 (shape n at n * 64): the Vic Viper level ($80) and banked ($84-$87; ship_shapes), an Option ($81), and with the shield ($82, $83). The falling wreck reuses the banked shapes.
Shapes $88-$89: the Options glowing (option_shades).
Shapes $8A-$8D: the walkers on the ceiling, the floor walker's four shapes ($9B-$9E) drawn upside down. Seen in play on stages 1 and 4, in the colours the walking events give (red and orange).
Shapes $8E-$90: the homing enemies, level, leaning up and leaning down.
Shapes $91-$94: the wave enemies' four-step animation.
Shape $95: the plain aimed bullet.
Shapes $96-$99: the crawlers' four-step animation.
Shape $9A: a tall frame; no mover found using it.
Shapes $9B-$9E: the walkers stepping ($9B-$9D) and standing ($9E).
Shape $9F: a solid block; no mover found using it.
Shapes $A0-$A3: the hoppers' animation.
Shapes $A4-$A5: the enemy hatch shut, on the floor and on the ceiling.
Shape $A6: the ring bullet of stage 3.
Shapes $A7-$AC: the six parts of the Big Core, drawn double size.
Rows 19 and 20 of the Big Core's shape $A7, where core_walls_draw writes the walls as they are shot away (and $2A80, rows 0 and 1 of shape $AA).
The second byte of each wall row in shape $A7.
The end of shape $A8 and all of shape $A9, parts of the Big Core.
Rows 0 and 1 of shape $AA, the other end of the Big Core's walls.
The second byte of each wall row in shape $AA.
Shapes $AB and $AC, the last two parts of the Big Core, from the fourth byte of $AB.
Shapes $AD-$AF: rocks thrown by the volcanoes.
Shapes $B0-$B2: the hatch's explosion.
Shapes $B3-$BA: the hatch opening, $B3-$B6 on the floor and $B7-$BA on the ceiling.
Shape $BB: the small cross-shaped bullet of stages 5 and 7.
Shapes $BC-$BF: the last boss, a square of four double-size sprites. clear_brain empties them and add_dot draws them in again dot by dot from $9C49, so what is here at the start is overwritten.
Shapes $C0-$C1: a block and a speckle; no mover found using them.
Shapes $C2-$C9: the aimed ball growing from $C8 down to $C2 before it sets off, and flying as $C2; $C9 is not used.
Shapes $CA-$CB: small craft; no mover found using them.
Shapes $CC-$CD: the exhaust flame behind the Vic Viper, short and long.
Shapes $CE-$D2: the swooping fliers' turn.
Shapes $D3-$D4: the big carrier, shut and open.
Shapes $D5-$D8: the darts of stage 4's attack, turning.
Shapes $D9-$DD: stage 6's pink sphere ($D9-$DA pulsing) and its dying frames.
Shape $DE: unused.
Shape $DF: a fragment of a bursting block.

The lower half of the character set ($3800, characters $00-$7F), the same on every stage: the power-up bar's letters ($00-$1D, drawn through extended colour as $80-$9D), the space ($20), the lives icon ($21-$22), the shots ($28-$2A), digits ($30-$39), HI ($3A-$3B), explosions, the laser ($58-$64), a second set of digits, the capsule ($78-$7B, animated by spin_capsules) and the stars. The upper half, $3C00-$3FFF, is copied in from the stage's own set (load_stage_charset).
Character $20, the space; on stage 8 irq_stage8 turns it into a dotted grid for the fortress.
Characters $78-$7B, the capsule, rewritten every fourth frame by spin_capsules.
The score of the player now playing, ten decimal digits from the most significant, one per byte. game_loop copies each player's ten digits in and out of score_store at $0200 around a turn.
The hundred-thousands digit of the score, which extra_life watches.
Finds the first non-zero digit of the score and carries on at $FF00, which prints it.
Leftover bytes that nothing runs: the end of an older score printer (ADC #$30, STA $0429,Y, ten digits).
Adds one to the eighth score digit, which is the hundreds, carrying up through the digits to the second (the carry never reaches the first).
Adds A hundreds to the score, one at a time through add_100. Keeps X and Y.
Holds X across add_points.
Holds Y across add_points.
Sprite table, low byte of X, one per slot 0 to 7. Slot 0 is the Vic Viper. The tables that follow are indexed the same way and copied to the video chip each frame by draw_sprites.
X of sprite slot 1, the Big Core's first part, for core_shots.
X of sprite slot 3, the Big Core's third part.
X of sprite slot 7, the last Option.
Sprite table, Y position of each slot.
Y of sprite slot 1, the Big Core's first part, which core_bob moves it by.
Y of sprite slot 7.
Sprite table, ninth bit of X, 0 or 1.
X high bit of sprite slot 1.
X high bit of sprite slot 3.
X high bit of sprite slot 7.
Sprite table, each slot's colour.
Colour of sprite slot 7.
Sprite table, non-zero to draw the slot at double width and height.
Sprite table, non-zero to draw the slot in multicolour.
Sprite table, the shape's first pointer value; spr_anim is added to it.
Shape of sprite slot 7.
Sprite table, the animation step added to spr_frame.
Sprite table, non-zero when the slot is in use.
Whether sprite slot 7 is in use.

Rebuilds the video chip's sprites from the sprite tables: clears enables, ninth bits, expansion and multicolour, then hands each slot that is on to draw_sprite. Slots in use take the hardware sprites in order, so a gap in the tables leaves no gap in the hardware.
Puts sprite table slot X into the next free hardware sprite: position, enable bit, ninth X bit, expansion, multicolour, colour, and the shape pointer at $07F8 (spr_frame plus spr_anim).
The eight bit masks $01 to $80, one per sprite.
Twice the number of hardware sprites draw_sprites has filled, the offset into $D000.
The Vic Viper's X, low byte.
The Vic Viper's X, ninth bit.
The Vic Viper's Y.
Set to 1 when the Vic Viper is hit, by a sprite collision (check_collisions) or by the scenery at $56DA; the play loop reads it each pass.
The character move_fans is drawing for a flier, counting up across its cells.
Frames until launch_fans sends the next formation.
Set when the explosion about to start should leave a capsule behind.
Low byte of the screen address of each of the 25 rows.
High byte of the screen address of each row ($04 to $07).
Points $FB/$FC at the screen cell in column cell_x of row cell_y, using the row-address tables at $415C and $4176. Keeps X; returns Y = 0.
Holds X across screen_addr.
Column for screen_addr.
High byte of an X position passed with cell_x to spawn routines.
Row for screen_addr.
Fills screen memory $0400-$07FF with spaces ($20). Ends with Y = 0.
One colour per screen row, painted into colour RAM by stage_setup; loaded per stage.
The power-up bar's 37 character codes as drawn along screen row 23: the words SPEEDUP, MISSILE, DOUBLE, LASER, MULTI and ? in the bar's own letters ($80 up), with $24 between boxes.
A second copy of the bar's character codes, the same layout.
The column at which each of the six power-up boxes starts on row 23 (the screen's last row but one, $0798).
Which power-up box is lit, 0 to 5, or $FF for none. Each ordinary capsule the Vic Viper picks up moves it one box on; the blue one leaves it.
Redraws the power-up bar on row 23: copies bar_text to the screen and colours every cell black except the $73 cells, then paints the lit box (powerup_pos) red.
Each shot's screen column.
The missiles' columns: shot_col's slots 9 to 11.
The Vic Viper's character shots, nine slots: each one's screen row; 0 when free. Slots 0-5 take ordinary shots, 6-8 the DOUBLE shots.
The missiles' rows: shot_row's slots 9 to 11; 0 when free.
random's running sum.
random's counter, one more each call.
The range random was asked for.

Returns a pseudo-random number from 0 to A-1 in A. Mixes a running sum, a counter, the joystick port, a seed byte and a byte of the table at $A000, then takes it modulo A by repeated subtraction. Keeps X.
X kept by random.
The column of each of twinkle's twelve background stars; the first also stirs random.
The row of each twinkling star.
Calls left before twinkle moves a star: 3.
Every third call, takes one of twelve background stars at random, erases it if it is still a star character ($4B), and puts it at a new random cell.
Thrown objects, X low byte, eight slots.
Thrown objects, Y; 0 for a free slot.
Thrown objects, X ninth bit.
Thrown objects, upward speed, taken from Y each frame; negative values fall.
Thrown objects, sideways speed.
Thrown objects, the sprite slot each rides.
Thrown objects, 1 to move right, 0 to move left.
Thrown objects, frames left before the upward speed drops by one.

Moves up to eight thrown objects, each riding a sprite slot: X goes left or right by its speed, Y climbs by a speed that falls by one every four frames, so each flies in an arc. One that leaves rows $52-$DB is switched off with its sprite.

Starts a thrown object if a sprite slot (1 to 6) and an object slot are free: a random direction, sideways speed 0-3 and upward speed 3-7, from Y $B0 and one of two X positions, with one of three random shapes and colours; plays sound 6. In the stages that erupt, these are the volcanoes' rocks.
The two X positions (less 16) that thrown objects start from.
The three colours a thrown object can take.
Code that nothing calls: a loop that sets up the Big Core (core_setup) and runs its movement, lasers and sprites once a frame, as if to test it on its own.
X of each of the six sprites that make up the Big Core, three across and two down.
Y of each of the six.
Shape of each of the six.

Builds the Big Core, the end-of-stage boss: resets its core walls (core_walls_reset) and the dissolve (dissolve_reset), then puts its six parts in sprite slots 1 to 6, doubled in size, blue, at the right of the screen, and sets it entering.
The Big Core's state: 1 while it slides in from the right, 3 once in place and moving up and down.
Each frame of the Big Core: runs the dissolve, then in state 1 slides all six parts left a pixel until they reach X $126, then switches to state 3; in state 3 moves them up and down (core_bob).
Code that nothing calls: raises the Big Core's six parts a pixel until the second reaches Y $64, then sets core_state to 2, a state nothing else uses.
State 1 of core_move: slides the six parts left a pixel, and once the first is at X $126 switches to state 3.
Frames left before the Big Core next chooses which way to move.
Counts the Big Core's turns; it moves only on odd counts.
The Big Core's vertical step: 1 down, -1 up.

The Big Core's vertical movement: every 16 frames turns toward the Vic Viper (down while the ship is lower than the core), then on odd turns moves its six parts a pixel, staying between Y $4C and $8C.
The four core lasers' columns.
The four core lasers' rows; 0 when off.
How far right of column 22 each laser starts.
How far below the core's row each laser starts.
Frames until the Big Core fires again.

The Big Core's four lasers, drawn in characters: every 60 frames, once the core is in place, starts four three-character beams level with it; each frame moves each beam a column left, erasing its old cells, until it reaches the left edge.
The shapes of the Big Core's walls at each stage of damage, eight bytes a stage, written into its sprite shapes at $29F9 and $2A80.
The second half of each damage stage's eight bytes, written to $29FC and $2A80.
How many of the Big Core's walls have been shot away, 0 to 5; $FF when no core is on screen.
Sets core_hits to 0 and draws the walls whole.
Writes the wall shape for the current damage into the core's two sprite shapes.
A shot reached the core: adds one to core_hits, plays sound 4 and redraws the walls; at 5 the core is destroyed.
Starts the dissolve at the first character and the first pixel pair.
Which of the four two-bit pixel positions the dissolve is clearing.
The address the dissolve works on, in the characters from $3C00 to $3CFF.
High byte of dissolve_ptr: $3C.
Which of eight rows (in a scattered order) the dissolve is clearing in each character.

One step of the dissolve that wipes the background as the Big Core arrives: clears one pixel pair in one row of one character at $3C00-$3CFF, moving eight bytes on each call. After the four pixel positions of every row the characters are blank, and the stage's rows are cleared from the screen (clear_rows).
The four two-pixel masks the dissolve clears, in turn.
The mask that keeps the other pixels.
The order in which the dissolve takes the eight rows of a character.
Moves the dissolve on a row; after eight rows a pass, and after four passes it is finished (state 2), and the rows are cleared once (state 1).
Runs dissolve_step 20 times; called once a frame.
0 while the dissolve runs, 2 when it has just finished, 1 when the rows are cleared.
Blanks the seven screen rows listed in rows_to_clear: the top row of play and the six above the bar.
The rows clear_rows blanks: 3 and 15 to 21.
The sprite slot of each of three homing enemies, $FF when the slot is free.
The second homer's sprite slot.
The third homer's sprite slot.
The rows (Y) the three homing enemies start at.
The X positions (above 256) they start at.
Starts a group of three homing enemies at the right edge, in the colour given in A, each in the next free sprite slot from 1 to 6, with shape $8E.
Colour for the enemies a spawn routine starts.
Which of the three homing enemies may steer this time; moves to the next every 12 frames.
Frames left before homer_turn moves on.

Moves the three homing enemies two pixels left a frame; the one whose turn it is also climbs or dives two pixels toward the Vic Viper's height, with a shape that leans up ($8F) or down ($90). One that leaves at the left, is switched off, or has become an explosion (shape $95) frees its slot.
22 heights of a sine-like wave, 0 to 30, that the wave enemies add to their starting row.
The shape each wave enemy shows at each point of the wave, $91 to $94.
Where each of the two wave enemies is in the wave, counted in half steps up to 44.
The rows the two wave enemies start at.
The sprite slot of each of the two wave enemies, $FF when free.
The second wave enemy's sprite slot.
Starts two wave enemies at the right edge (X $158), in the colour given in A.
Moves the two wave enemies two pixels left a frame while they rise and fall through the wave, changing shape with it; frees one that leaves at the left or has been shot.
Keeps Y while move_wavers reads the wave.
Hopping enemies (four slots), Y; 0 when the slot is free.
Hopping enemies, X low byte.
Hopping enemies, X ninth bit.
Hopping enemies, sideways step each frame: 4 to the right, or $FB (five to the left).
Hopping enemies, upward speed, taken from Y each frame and reduced by one every five frames, so they fall back.
Hopping enemies, an animation counter; its bits pick shapes $A0 to $A3.
Hopping enemies, frames left before the upward speed drops.
Starts a hopper at cell_x (high byte in $41AE) on the ground (Y $C8) in colour A, hopping right with speed 4 from the left edge or left with speed 5 from the right.
The colour spawn_hopper was given.
Fills a free hopper slot (see spawn_hopper).
Hopping enemies, the sprite slot each rides.

Moves the four hopping enemies: each flies in an arc under its falling speed, and when it lands on scenery (a character $80 or above under it) bounces up with speed 5, plays sound 7, and turns to hop toward the Vic Viper's column. One that rises above row $52 has its speed reversed. One that leaves at either side, or whose sprite has been switched off, is freed.
The Vic Viper's screen column, worked out from its X at the start of move_hoppers.
Frees the hopper and its sprite.
Walking enemies (two slots), X.
Walking enemies, Y; 0 when free.
The second walker's Y.
Walking enemies, 0 while walking right along the scenery, $FA once it has reached the right side and walks left with the scroll.
Walking enemies, the shape, $9B to $9D as it walks; $9E when it stops.

Moves the two walking enemies along the ground or the ceiling: each steps two pixels right with a three-frame walk, follows the scenery up or down a character to stay on its surface, and turns back at X $F8. A walker in the top half of the screen (Y below $64) takes the upside-down shapes, $11 lower. Frees one whose sprite has gone.
An unused byte before move_walkers' last RTS.
Returns from move_walkers.
Walking enemies, the sprite slot each rides.
The second walker's sprite slot.
Starts a walker at row A on the right (X $22, in its own units) in the event's colour, if a sprite slot and one of two walker slots are free.
Walking enemies, frames left before the next step of the walk.
The colour the next walker is given, from the event that sends it.
The stage being played, 0 to 7.
Frames left of the Vic Viper's flash.
The character move_missiles draws a missile with.
Power-up capsules, up to ten (capsule_count of them are read): each one's row; 0 when free. A capsule is a block of four characters, $78-$7B.
Each capsule's column.
Each capsule's colour: 15 for an ordinary capsule, 14 for the blue one that clears the screen.
How many capsule slots are in use: 4.

Scrolls the playfield one character left: copies each of the 19 rows from 3 to 21, columns 1 to 39, one place to the left. The new right-hand column is drawn next frame (map_column). Colour RAM is not moved here; recolour_row and recolour_blocks keep it right.
Pixels the Vic Viper moves left or right each step; SPEEDUP raises it.
Pixels it moves up or down each step.
Reads joystick port 2 and moves the Vic Viper: up, down, right, left (ship_up and the rest), and fire (fire_button). Releasing fire clears fire_held.
Moves the Vic Viper up by ship_speed_y unless it is at the top (Y $4E); sets ship_moved and the tilt.
Which way the ship last moved vertically: $FF up, 1 down, 0 level; picks its banked shape.
Moves the Vic Viper down unless it is at the bottom (Y $CB).
Moves the Vic Viper right unless it is at the right edge (X $12C).
Moves the Vic Viper left unless it is at the left edge (X $38).
Frames before the Vic Viper can fire again.
Frames left in the hold that stops held fire from firing every frame; letting go clears it.
Fire is down: if both counters are clear, fires (fire_shot), sets both to 16 and plays sound 3; otherwise counts them down. Held, the ship fires every 17 frames.
Spare bytes after fire_button.
The keyboard controls, read beside the joystick: Z left, X right, ; up, / down, RETURN fire, and right SHIFT to take the lit power-up (take_powerup).
Set when the Vic Viper moved this frame; the options then follow (options_follow).
One step of the player's controls: reads the joystick and the keys, copies the ship's position into sprite slot 0, sets its shape (ship_shape), and when it moved, records the move for the options.
Set when the ship moved right this frame.
Where the next column of the stage's map is read, low byte.
Where the next column of the stage's map is read, high byte.
Screen address (low byte) of the right-hand cell of each playfield row, 20 entries for rows 3 to 22: map_column fills the first 19, and map_gap_down reads the 20th.
Screen address (high byte) of the same cells.

Draws the stage's next column at the right edge of rows 3 to 21 from the map. The map is a stream of bytes: a value of $7F or more is a character to place in the next row; a smaller value is a count of empty rows to fill with spaces. When the 19 rows are filled the pointer moves past what it read.
Bytes of the map read for this column.
A gap count in the map: that many spaces, going down.
Spaces left to place for a run of empty rows.
Each shot's kind: 1 for an ordinary shot, which moves two columns a frame along its row; 2 for a DOUBLE shot, which moves one column right and one row up.

Moves the Vic Viper's shots, which are characters on the screen, not sprites. Each erases its old cell and moves on; it is drawn as character $29, or $28 for the rising DOUBLE shot. A shot that meets solid scenery (a character from $80 up to scenery_limit), passes column 38 or leaves rows 4 to 20 is freed, and one that hits scenery plays sound 7.
The first slot for each kind of shot: 0 for ordinary shots, 6 for DOUBLE shots.

Starts a shot of the kind in A (1 ordinary, 2 DOUBLE) at the position in cell_x, cell_y and the X high byte, in the first free slot of its kind. Ordinary shots may have twice shot_limit on screen, DOUBLE shots shot_limit. The pixel position becomes a cell: X over 8, less 3, and (Y - 42) over 8.
How many shots each emitter may have on screen: the number of emitters, the ship plus its options.
The number of slots start_shot may search for this kind of shot.
Fills shot slot X from the firing point: column and row from its X and Y, and its kind.
The kind of shot start_shot is placing.
The Vic Viper's five shapes, from banked hard down ($87) through level ($80) to banked hard up ($85).
Which of ship_shapes the ship shows, 0 to 4.
For each bank, the next one on the way back to level.
Frames until the bank changes again.
Every six frames tilts the Vic Viper one step toward its direction of travel (up or down), or back toward level when it is not moving vertically, and sets its shape in sprite slot 0.
Blanks the right-hand column of rows 3 to 21, in place of a map column when there is no scenery.
Set while the stage's map is being drawn; clear in open space, when the right-hand column is blanked instead.
Draws the next map column at the right edge (map_column), or a blank one when scenery_on is clear.
The address in new_column's JSR, which pick_column_drawer sets to map_column or map_column_up.
High byte of the column drawer's address.
Returns from new_column.

Low bytes of where each stage's map starts. Stages 1 and 4 share $A000. Stage 6's entry points at stage 2's map ($AD00), but its event list never turns the scenery on, so that map is never drawn there.
High bytes of the map starts.
Event 1: turns the scenery on and points the map at the stage's start (map_starts).
Set once the player has taken MISSILE: each shot also drops a missile.
Set once the player has taken DOUBLE: each shot also fires a rising shot.
Set once the player has taken LASER: shots are lasers instead of ordinary shots.
Code that nothing calls: copies the Vic Viper's position into cell_x, cell_y and the X high byte, the setup fire_from_point needs, as if from a version that fired only from the ship.
Fires from one point (cell_x, cell_y): a laser if the player has LASER, otherwise an ordinary shot; a DOUBLE shot as well if they have DOUBLE; and a missile if they have MISSILE.
Starts a laser at the point in cell_x and cell_y in the first free laser slot, up to shot_limit.
The character the laser being drawn uses.
Lasers, three slots: the column of each one's start.
The second laser's column.
The third laser's column.
Lasers, each one's Y as a pixel row less 40; 0 when free.
The second laser's row.
The third laser's row.

Moves the three lasers. Each erases its old span of laser_length cells (stopping at solid scenery, though character $96 does not stop it), moves three columns right, and draws the span again in colour 11 with the last cell in colour 9. The laser character is $5C plus the low three bits of its pixel row, so the beam sits at the ship's exact height inside the character. A laser that meets solid scenery or passes column 36 is freed.
Cells of the laser span still to erase or draw.
Frees the laser slot.

Takes the power-up whose box is lit (powerup_pos), as right SHIFT does from the keyboard. SPEEDUP adds one to both ship speeds, up to 4. MISSILE gives missiles, and a second MISSILE makes them move every frame instead of every other. DOUBLE gives the rising shot and takes LASER away; LASER gives lasers and takes DOUBLE away, each putting back the other's box. MULTI adds an option, up to two. ? gives the shield, four hits' worth. A power-up that can go no further has its box blanked (bar_blank), and once a box is blank, choosing it does nothing. Taking one turns the bar off, plays sound 1 and redraws the bar.
How many more hits the Vic Viper can take: set to 4 by the ? power-up; the play loop takes one off for each hit, and a collision with a big sprite empties it.
How many cells long a laser is: 5.
The SPEEDUP power-up: adds one to the ship's speed, up to 4.
Fills one power-up box (five characters from offset X in bar_text) with character $23, so the word no longer shows.
Frames between missile steps: 2 after the first MISSILE, 1 after the second.
Frames left before the missiles next move.

Moves the missiles, which use shot slots 9 to 11 (rows at $4280, columns at $4274). Each erases its cell and moves one column right and one row down, as character $2A; where the cell below is solid it stays on its row instead, as character $29, so it runs along the ground. A missile that hits scenery (sound 7), leaves rows 3 to 20 or passes column 37 is freed.

Characters from $80 up to this value, less one, are solid scenery that stops the Vic Viper's shots, lasers and missiles; characters from here up are background they pass through. $AB on most stages, $F0 on the sixth (index 5). The ship itself collides with any character from $90 up (scenery_touch).
Frees the missile slot.
Starts a missile in the first free slot of 9 to 11, at the point start_shot is given.
The Vic Viper's last 16 positions, X low byte. The options follow seven and fourteen steps behind.
The same, X ninth bit.
The same, Y.
Index of the newest entry in the trail (low four bits).
Called when the ship moves: adds its position to the trail.
How many points fire at once: 1 for the ship, plus one for each option.
Index into the ship's trail of the point now firing.
Points still to fire this shot.
Fires a volley: from the Vic Viper's place in its trail and from each option's, seven steps further back each time, calls fire_from_point for every one.
The colour RAM address of the row recolour_row repaints next.
High byte of recolour_ptr.
The row recolour_row repaints next.

Repaints one row of colour RAM a call, moving down rows 3 to 21 and back to 3: every cell that holds a space, a character below $80, or a character from scenery_limit up gets the row's colour from row_colours. The colours do not scroll with the characters, so this keeps the background and shots in their row's colour while solid scenery keeps the colours it was drawn with.
Keeps the colour RAM under each capsule right as the playfield scrolls: for a capsule within three rows of the row recolour_row is on, paints its four cells in its colour.
A spare zero after recolour_capsules.

Stage 4's map drawer: the same as map_column but filling the column from the bottom row up. Stage 4 points at the same map as stage 1 ($A000, map_starts), so it is stage 1 drawn upside down, the volcanoes hanging from the ceiling.
A gap count in the map: that many spaces, going up.
Points the JSR in new_column at the map drawer for this stage: map_column on every stage except the fourth (index 3), which has a drawer of its own at $54DF.
Leftover bytes that nothing runs: an older copy of the end of draw_blocks and the start of burst_block, with its last JSR cut off.
The playfield's background colour, written to $D021 by the interrupt; set to 1 (white) for a flash.

Moves each capsule one column left and draws it again: characters $78-$7B over two rows and two columns, the left pair in the capsule's colour and the right in the row's colour. One that reaches column 0 is erased (erase_capsule).
Blanks capsule X's four cells and frees the slot.
Counts capsules dropped; every seventh is the blue one.
Leaves a capsule at the cell in cell_x and cell_y, if it lies between columns 2 and 35 and a slot is free. Every seventh capsule dropped is blue (colour 14), the rest are ordinary (colour 15).
The colour of the capsule being dropped.
The nine cells round the Vic Viper that scenery_touch reads: three columns across and three rows down from its top-left cell.
1 for the cells of the middle row, where scenery is deadly; 0 for the rest, which only collect capsules.

Finds the Vic Viper's cell from its position and reads the nine cells round it. A character from $90 up in the middle row sets ship_hit. A capsule character in any of the nine collects that capsule (collect_capsule).
The four characters of a capsule, top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right.
How far each capsule character is from the capsule's left column.
How far each is from its top row.
Column offset of each of the nine cells scenery_touch reads.
Row offset of each.
The ship has touched a capsule character: works out the capsule's top-left cell from which character it touched, finds that capsule, erases it, gives its power (capsule_power) and scores 500.

An ordinary capsule moves the lit box of the power-up bar one on (from none to SPEEDUP, and from ? back round to SPEEDUP) and plays sound 0. The blue capsule destroys the enemies on screen instead (blue_capsule).
The colour of the capsule just collected.
Takes the lit box off the power-up bar.
Character-drawn formation enemies, twelve slots in two groups of six (0-5 and 6-11): each one's column.
Each flier's row.
Each one's state: 0 free, 1 flying, 2 waiting to enter.
Six bytes that stage_setup clears with the other objects' tables and nothing else touches, then seven spare zeros.
The formations' flight script: indices into fan_dx and fan_dy, one per leg, each script ending in $FF. Group A's starts at 0, group B's at 12.
How many steps each leg of the script lasts (indexed like fan_moves); $FF sends a flier back to the start of the script.
Each flier's steps left in its leg, or, while waiting, before it enters.
The waits before each of the six fliers in a group enters, so they come in one behind another.
Cleared at the start of move_fans; nothing reads it.
Where each flier is in the script.
The leg each flier starts on: 0 for group A, 12 for group B.
Column step for each direction of the script.
Each flier's animation counter; its low two bits pick the shape.
Row step for each direction.
The four first characters of a flier's animation; each shape is four characters from there, two by two.
Toggles which group move_fans moves, so each moves every second call.
Counts the six fliers of the group being moved.
The column each flier enters at.
The entry columns as reset_fans_a copies them.
The row each flier enters at.
The entry rows as reset_fans_a copies them.
0 for the fliers of group A, 1 for group B.
How many of each group's six have been shot; the sixth leaves a capsule.
The second group's kills.
The Vic Viper's screen row, for the fliers' turn toward it.

Moves one group of six character-drawn fliers (the two groups take turns). A waiting flier counts down and enters at its start cell. A flying one erases its four cells, keeping two of the characters it covered so a laser there can be seen (fan_lasered), follows its script one cell a step, turns at the Vic Viper's row when it reaches the leg that waits for it, and is drawn again as four animated characters in colour 14. One that leaves the playfield is freed.
Looks for one of the twelve shot and missile slots within a cell of cell_x, cell_y (same row or the one below, same column or the one to the right). Returns the slot in A, or $FF if none. Keeps X.
Holds X across shot_at.

An enemy has been destroyed at cell_x, cell_y: scores 100 unless the ship is exploding, and starts an explosion there in a free explosion slot (after clearing the oldest with explosions_reset when none is free). The explosion keeps the four characters it covers that are background (from $27 to $7F) so it can put them back.
Holds X across enemy_destroyed.
Holds Y across enemy_destroyed.
Fills explosion slot X at cell_x, cell_y for 11 frames, keeping the background characters under its four cells so they can be put back.
Reads the character at offset Y from the cell: returns it if it is background ($27-$7F, below scenery_limit), or a space if it is anything else.
Explosions, the character each one covers at its top left.
The character each covers at its bottom left.
The character each covers at its top right.
The character each covers at its bottom right.
Puts group A's six fliers (slots 0-5) back waiting at their entry cells with their delays and first leg.
The same for group B (slots 6-11).
Counts formations launched; its low bit picks the group.
Formations launched this stage; at 10 no more come. $0B (more than 10) stops them altogether.
The two characters move_fans found under a flier's right-hand cells.
The second character under the flier.
Every 140 frames sends the next formation of six fliers, group A and group B by turns, until ten have come.
Returns non-zero, and destroys the flier, if either character it covered was part of a laser beam ($5B-$63).

Destroys flier X: erases its four cells, counts the kill in its group (the sixth kill of a group makes its explosion leave a capsule), calls enemy_destroyed, frees the slot and plays sound 4. Returns 1.
Holds X across kill_fan.
Tests each flying flier against the Vic Viper's shots and missiles; one that is hit loses its shot and is destroyed.
Explosions, up to four (explosion_slots): each one's column.
Each explosion's row.
Frames left in each explosion, 11 down to 1; 0 when free.
For each frame of an explosion (indexed by boom_time), the first of the four characters drawn, two by two: $58, $54, $50 and $4C as it fades.
The character move_explosions draws at the top left.
At the top right.
At the bottom left.
At the bottom right.
Set for an explosion that leaves a capsule when it ends.
The colour of each frame of an explosion, flickering between red, yellow and white.
The colour move_explosions paints this frame.
Draws each explosion's next frame: four characters and their colours, counting down. On the last frame it puts back the four background characters it covered, and drops a capsule if it was marked to.
The loop step of move_explosions.

The blue capsule's power, destroying the enemies on screen. Every sprite enemy in slots 1-6 that is not already exploding, not a big sprite and not off the right edge is destroyed where it stands (a red one, colour 2, leaves a capsule); so are the three objects at $61CB, the six at $7067 and every flier that has entered. Then the background flashes white and fades (bg_flash) and sound 5 plays.
How many explosion slots enemy_destroyed searches: 4.
When no explosion slot is free: drops the capsule if one was due, otherwise blanks the 2x2 cells at once.
Which of the six heads head_fire looks at this call; it goes round all six.

Fifth-stage heads (the stage whose routine is $6DC8), six slots: a head that has scrolled past column 38 is freed; one whose mouth timer is running counts it down, and below 60 fires a ring from its mouth (fire_ring). Every 5 to 14 calls a random head whose timer is idle is set to open its mouth (timer 8).
Calls until head_fire next picks a head to open its mouth.
Screen offsets of the four cells, one under another, that head_hits tests.

Tests the column two to the left of each head on four rows for one of the Vic Viper's shots or missiles ($28-$2A) or a laser ($5B-$63). Each hit takes one from the head's strength and makes a small explosion; at 0 the head is erased (all 24 of its cells), scores 1200, plays sound 5 and leaves a capsule.
Holds X across head_hits.
One hit on a head: takes one of its ten, with a small explosion; the tenth rubs out its 24 cells, scores 1200 points with sound 5, and leaves a capsule.
The screen offsets of a head's 24 cells, six across and four down.
Stage 5's attack mover (attack_movers): draws the bursting blocks and moves their fragments.

Code that nothing calls: a game for one player that zeroes the score, gives three lives and plays from the stage in old_start_stage, moving on when a stage is cleared and ending when the lives run out. It looks like the one-player loop that game_loop replaced.
The stage old_game_start begins on.
The lives of the player now playing.
Draws up to three Vic Viper icons (characters $21 and $22) at the top left of the screen, one per life.
Icons still to draw.
Set to 11 by stage_setup; title_stars draws stars only while it is non-zero.
Each stage's first shared multicolour ($D022).
Each stage's second shared multicolour ($D023).
Each stage's value for $924A, read by the enemy-fire routine.

Non-zero while the title runs: stage_setup clears it, and title_stars then does not twinkle.
For each of the three hatch-like objects, the rows below its top at which it fires.

Moves the twelve stars of the title's star field left by each one's speed, erasing each at its old cell and drawing it at the new one; a star that leaves the screen comes back at the right on a random row with a random speed. Set when the stage's scenery has run out and the boss is due: the title's star field takes over the background, and boss_phase runs.

On every stage but the last, twinkles the background stars as well.
Puts the Vic Viper back at the start of a life: no missiles, DOUBLE, laser, shield or Options, speed 1, at X $64, Y $8C, with its whole trail at that point.
Which of the three turrets turret_aim works on this frame.

Turns one turret a frame toward the Vic Viper: by whether the ship is above, level with or below it (rows 9 and 16 the borders) and whether it is right or left, picks one of six barrel pictures, and for a turret of the other kind ($C8) six more, and draws the barrel's two characters. Left barrel character to draw.
Right barrel character to draw.
Counts 2, 1: scroll_step and others use it to work on every other frame.
The shape the hatch is given this frame.
Frames until the hatch has opened: from 40, its last six frames stepping through the opening shapes.

Starts an enemy hatch at the right edge (X $150) on row cell_y, $B0 on the floor or $52 on the ceiling (events 17 and 18), freeing any double-size sprite first. It takes eight hits; release_rushers lets rushers out of it while it lasts.
Hits the hatch can still take: 8.
Shapes of the hatch's explosion, one a frame for ten frames.
The hatch's shape before it opens.
High byte of the hatch's X.
Looks at the four cells of each turret for a shot ($28-$2A) or laser ($58-$64): a hit destroys the turret (sound 4) with an explosion, which leaves a capsule if the turret was colour 10.
Screen offsets of a turret's four cells.

The hatch's Y; 0 when there is none. Below $80 it is on the ceiling.
Low byte of the hatch's X.
The hatch's colour.

The laser half of hatch_hits_test.
Copies the power-up bar's text back (from bar_text_2) and clears the bar's lit box.
Runs moai_hit_test for every Moai whose mouth is open.
Set while stage 4's volcano is on screen and erupting.
Event 24: starts the volcano at the right edge (X $150).
Stage 4's attack mover: sends and moves the darts and tests them against the player's shots.
Each frame of stage 4: moves the volcano left with the scenery (a pixel every other frame) and erupts, until it passes X $18; and moves its rocks.
Stage 6's spheres: sends new ones while sphere_spawn is set, and moves them.
Set while stage 6 sends pink spheres; event 25 turns it on and off.
Event 25: turns sending pink spheres on or off.

The interrupt work every stage shares: the player's controls, $6B8B, the Options and exhaust, $774C, $7809, $695B, a step of restoring swapped characters, the shots against the fliers, the capsule's animation, and the Q key.

Stage 8's phase-2 interrupt work: the usual movers, and once the stage reaches map position $0128 the space character becomes a dotted grid (a byte of $55 and seven of $01) and the star field stops twinkling (title_flag), for the fortress.
Leftover bytes after irq_stage8 that nothing runs.
Event 26: a head rising out of the floor at column 32, at the row the event's next extra gives (add_head, type 0).
Event 27: a head coming down from the ceiling (add_head, type 1).
Stage 5's phase-2 interrupt work: the stage 3 work (irq_stage3) and the wave enemies every other frame.
Frames until irq_stage5 moves the wave enemies again: every other frame.
Fills the first three and last three rows of the screen with character $24 in blue.
Leftover code that nothing calls: an older copy of the end of fill_borders, edging the screen with characters $68-$70. A stray byte at $6918 breaks its loop, so it would not run as it stands.
Frames until a sprite enemy may fire again: 40.

Every 40 frames, on stages whose bullets are the plain shape $95, picks a random sprite slot 1 to 6 and, if it holds a small enemy (not a bullet, not a double-size sprite) on the playfield, fires an aimed bullet from it.
Fires an aimed bullet from column 27 at a random row 15 to 21, keeps stage 7's attack going, and flashes the target (flash_target).

Stage 7's attack starter: the boss block. Fires (core7_fire), then counts any shot or laser in the block's six cells at $05D1 as a hit (sound 6); at 40 hits the attack ends and the block's rows are cleared.
Screen offsets of the six cells of stage 7's boss block.
One hit on stage 7's boss block (sound 6, a flash); at 40 it ends the attack and clears the block's seven rows.

Colours the block's three rows by target_flash from target_colours, counting the flash down.
Frames left of the block's flash after a hit.
Colours of the block's flash.
Hits stage 7's boss block has taken; at 40 it is destroyed.
Stage 8's attack mover (attack_movers): each frame of the last fight runs final_fight and ends the stage once brain_dead is set.

The work of stage 8, run on 14 frames in 16 (all but the two on which scroll_step draws the new column and shifts the map), and not in boss mode: the formations, the ring firers, the player's weapons and the stage's own work.
A lone RTS that the play frame calls at $688E. The two bytes after it are $B9 $6A: with $4C (JMP) in place of the RTS this would be JMP music_key, so one byte seems to have switched the M key off.
The address operand left behind the RTS at jmp_music_key: $6AB9, music_key.
When music is on (music_on), steps the volume fade and the tune player. Nothing calls it.

1 when the game should play its tune instead of sound effects; the effects player (play_effect) stays silent while it is set. Cleared at the start of each turn and kept per player at $0267, but the M key that sets it is switched off (jmp_music_key), so it stays 0.
Set while M is held, so one press toggles music_on once.

Toggles music_on when M is pressed (row 4, column 4 of the keyboard), and once more only after it has been let go. Its only way in is cut off (jmp_music_key); with the RTS there changed to JMP it works.
Puts character $24 at the screen's top-left corner, whichever way music_on is set: a marker for the music switch, now the same both ways. Called as each life starts.
M is up: clears m_held.
Q (row 7, column 6 of the keyboard) gives up the game: lives drop to 1, cheat_mode is cleared and turn_over is set, so the turn ends and with it the player's last life.

Leftover code that nothing calls: a pause on the P key. It switches the interrupt and the screen off, silences the SID, waits for P to be let go, pressed and let go again, then turns the screen and the interrupt back on. Its delay calls land in the middle of an instruction ($6B81), so it is not in a state to run.
Gives a life (sound 8) each time the score's hundred-thousands digit changes: an extra Vic Viper every 100,000 points.
The hundred-thousands digit when extra_life last looked.
Set while the Vic Viper's explosion falls: death_fall then runs in place of play_frame_common, while the other phase-2 movers carry on.

The raster interrupt's body. Acknowledges the video chip, keeps $FB-$FE and cell_x/cell_y for the main program, and steps a counter through four phases, one per interrupt, each setting the line for the next: phase 0 at line 40 turns extended colour off and draws the sprites; phase 1 at line 71 sets the playfield's colours and fine scroll; phase 2 at line 80 runs the game's movers; phase 3, asked for at line 224 but taken only when phase 2 has finished, sets the power-up bar's colours and extended colour and steps the scroll (scroll_step). Ends at irq_exit.
The address of the stage's phase-2 interrupt routine, written by set_stage_hooks.
High byte of the phase-2 routine's address.
Phase 3 of the interrupt: on to irq_bar.

Phase 1 of the interrupt: after a short delay sets the background colour, the next raster line ($50), the fine scroll and the two extra background colours; on the frame the scenery moves a whole character it moves the objects and capsules with it, otherwise it steps any background flash.
The colours a flash fades through, read backwards from bg_flash: white, yellow, light grey, grey, dark grey and black, with the stage's background first.
Entry 1 of flash_colours, the last colour of every flash, which stage_setup sets to black with entry 0.
Frames left in a background flash; each frame takes the next colour from flash_colours into bg_colour.
Phase 3 of irq_chain: blacks the background, turns on extended colour for the bar at the bottom, steps the scroll, and asks for line 40 for phase 0.
Phase 0 of irq_chain: turns extended colour off, blacks the border, draws the sprites, plays queued sound, and asks for line 71 for phase 1.
Unused bytes between irq_top's jump and the dead code after it: 8, 7, 7, 1, 1, 7, 7, 8.
Code that nothing calls: sets the raster line to $E1 and the phase counter to 1.
Where the dead code at $6C9B stores its phase counter: its own second byte.

Phase 2 of irq_chain: moves the ship (or, while it explodes, the explosion), then the enemies, shots and effects. Odd and even frames share the work: one half runs one set of movers, the other half the rest.
Counts interrupts; its low two bits pick the phase of irq_chain.
The playfield's fine horizontal scroll, 7 down to 0; it wraps from 0 back to 7 when the map moves a whole character.
Counts phase-2 interrupts, so once a frame; its low bit splits the movers between frames.

Every second frame steps scroll_x down a pixel: at 6 it draws the new column (new_column) and sets column_ready, at 7 it shifts the map a character (map_shift). On every other frame it runs the stage's own routine from stage_routines; in boss mode it runs boss_frame instead.
Set when scroll_step has shifted the map, cleared in phase 3; phase 0 then runs the work at $7307.
The routine each stage runs (by stage, two bytes each) on 14 frames in 16, through run_stage_routine: the enemy waves and the stage's own objects.
The high byte of each stage's routine, interleaved with stage_routines.
The stage's own routine, through stage_routines.
A spare RTS after the indirect jump.

The work of stage 1, run on 14 frames in 16 (all but the two on which scroll_step draws the new column and shifts the map), and not in boss mode: the rushers (rushers), the fliers' formations (launch_fans, move_fans), the ring firers, the player's weapons, the aimed bullets and $75B4.

The work of stage 2, run on 14 frames in 16 (all but the two on which scroll_step draws the new column and shifts the map), and not in boss mode: the ring firers, the formations, the player's weapons and the aimed bullets.

The work of stage 3, run on 14 frames in 16 (all but the two on which scroll_step draws the new column and shifts the map), and not in boss mode: the aimed bullets, the player's weapons and the swoopers.
Moves the player's lasers, missiles and shots, and tests the ship against the scenery.

The work of stage 4, run on 14 frames in 16 (all but the two on which scroll_step draws the new column and shifts the map), and not in boss mode: the aimed bullets, the ring firers, the formations, the rushers, the walkers ($681F), the player's weapons and $75B4.

The work of stage 6, run on 14 frames in 16 (all but the two on which scroll_step draws the new column and shifts the map), and not in boss mode: the tentacles (move_tentacles), the player's weapons and the aimed bullets.

The work of stage 5, run on 14 frames in 16 (all but the two on which scroll_step draws the new column and shifts the map), and not in boss mode: stage 3's work, then the heads ($1540, head_fire, head_hits) and the formations.
Each frame once the boss is due: the player's weapons and boss_phase.
The work of stage 7, run on 14 frames in 16 (all but the two on which scroll_step draws the new column and shifts the map), and not in boss mode: the formations and the player's weapons.

Starts a stage or a life: resets the ship and the power-up bar, then (at start_stage_run) sets up the stage, its characters, column drawer, swapped characters (except on stage 6), counters, event position ($8C), hooks, bar, score and lives, and turns the screen on.
The part of start_life that a cleared stage jumps to, keeping the ship's weapons.

The main program's loop during a stage: steps the ship's controls, the player's shots and the power-up bar, then the collision and pause tail. Leaves when the stage is cleared (stage_cleared), or when the ship has been hit and no shield is left (the death sequence starts), or when the game ends.

Set by the switched-off cheat_key. While it is set, play_loop skips its checks for a hit ship and a finished turn, so the ship cannot die, and the game ends after the turn instead of moving to the next player.
Set when the stage's boss is beaten; the play loop then moves to the next stage, after stage 8 back to stage 1 with the ending (ending).
Puts the KERNAL's IRQ address back in $0314 and turns off the raster interrupt.
A spare RTS after the play loop's jump.

When the scenery scrolls a whole character, moves every object drawn in characters one column left with it: shots, explosions, formations, rushers, lasers, ring firers, tentacles and loose pieces, and more.
Frame counter that picks which of the two uses slot 7 gets.

Shares sprite slot 7 between the Options (the glowing pods that follow the Vic Viper along its trail) and the exhaust: on even frames the first Option, eight steps back along the ship's trail; on odd frames the second, fourteen steps back, or when there is none and the ship is moving right, a flame behind it whose length grows with speed.
Eight frames of the Options' shape, cycled to make them glow.
The exhaust flame's colour, cycled through flame_colours.
Colours the flame flickers through: blue, purple, blue, light blue.
Frame counter for flame_colours.
Frame counter for option_shades.
The Options' shape this frame.
X of each of the six rushers, in half-columns.
Animation counter of each rusher.
First character of each of the rusher's four shapes ($CC, $D0, $D4, $D8), two by two characters each.
Each rusher's state: 1 flying left, 2 climbing, 3 diving, $FF free.
Half-column where the next rushers come out.
Row where the next rushers come out.
Counts 2, 1: the rushers move on every other frame.
Row of each rusher.
The Vic Viper's row, for the rushers to turn level at.

Moves the rushers, two-by-two character enemies in light blue: every other frame each moves half a column left and, while climbing or diving, a row toward the Vic Viper's row, flying level once it gets there (or at row 5 or 18). One that reaches the left edge is freed.
Frames until the next rusher comes out.
Rushers released from the current spawn point, up to four.
0 to start a new spawn point, 2 while releasing, 1 idle.

At a new spawn point (cell_x, cell_y) starts releasing; then every ten frames, while the spawn object is still there, lets out another rusher, four in all, climbing if the point is low on the screen and diving (with sound 6) if it is high.
Spare bytes after release_rushers.

Tests each small sprite enemy against the shots (shot_near) and lasers (laser_near): one that is hit is destroyed, a red one (colour 2) leaving a capsule. A struck enemy bullet ($BB or $A6) also frees its bullet slot.
Returns A = 0, and rubs the shot out, if a shot is within six columns and three rows of sprite X's cell (kept in near_col, near_row); otherwise 1.
Column of the sprite being tested.
Row of the sprite being tested.
Low bytes of the 32 event routines; the event's type indexes it.
High bytes of the event routines.
Low byte of how far the stage has scrolled, in characters; compared with each event's position.
High byte of event_pos.
Index of the stage's next event.

Runs every event due at the stage's present position: for each whose position (low byte at $8000, high at $8073) matches event_pos, puts its parameter ($815F) in event_colour and calls the routine its type ($80EC) names, through the JSR at $7330, whose address it writes. Then adds one to event_pos.
The JSR whose address run_events writes before each event.
The address operand of the JSR at $7330, written by run_events.
High byte of the event routine's address.
After each event: on to the next, and look again.

Event 5: a ring firer with characters $C4 at the row the event names, mouth offset 5.
