Event 19: rushers from column 35, row 6.
Index of the next event extra that event_extra hands out.
Returns the next byte of the stage's event extras ($81BB), stepping through them.
Event 8: a ring firer with characters $C8 at the row the event names, mouth offset 7.
The mouth offset given to the next ring firer.
Event 10: a hopper from the left edge in the event's colour, then one from the right (event 9).
Event 9: a hopper from the right edge (X $13C) in the event's colour.
Event 12: sets boss_mode, which hands the background to the star field, and starts the stage's attack for $350 frames (stage_attack).
Events 13 and 14: clears boss_mode.
High byte of the frames left of the stage's attack.
Low byte of the attack's countdown.

Runs the stage's attack while its countdown lasts: while more than $50 frames are left it calls the stage's starter (patched into the JSR at $7419 from attack_starters), and every frame the stage's mover (the JSR at $741C, from attack_movers). Stage 1 throws rocks, stage 2 aimed balls, stage 3 carriers, stage 4 patrolling darts, stage 5 bursting blocks, stage 8 the last boss. boss_phase calls it.
The address of the stage's attack starter, written by set_stage_hooks.
High byte of the attack starter's address.
The address of the stage's attack mover, written by set_stage_hooks.
High byte of the attack mover's address.
Marks the Big Core's build as under way.
Event: chooses tune 1 (set_tune) and clears fan_waves_left.
0 before the Big Core, 1 while it is built, 2 while it fights.

Event 16: chooses tune 2 (set_tune, which only clears the SID, as the tune never plays), turns the scenery on from the start of the stage's map (event_scenery), puts back the swapped characters and sets the stage's scenery limit.
A spare zero after start_tune2.
Event 17: an enemy hatch on the floor (spawn_hatch_sprite with Y $B0).
Event 18: an enemy hatch on the ceiling (spawn_hatch_sprite with Y $52).
Event 3: a group of three homing enemies in the event's colour.
Event 2: two wave enemies in the event's colour.
The volume of a fade-out, from 15 down to 0.
Frames left before fade_volume drops again.
While a fade runs (fade_volume not 0), lowers the SID volume by one every 20 frames, the first step after fade_delay frames, until it reaches 0. Only music_tick calls it.
Event 20: when music is on, starts a fade-out from volume 15, a step every 8 frames. As music is never on, it does nothing.
The sprite collision register as check_collisions read it.

Reads the video chip's sprite collision register. When the ship's sprite (bit 0) has touched another, finds each slot in use that collided and lies within 12 of the ship's X (in two-pixel units) and 21 of its Y, and on the first: sets ship_hit and plays sound 5. A slot that is a big sprite (spr_big) empties the shield count instead; any other slot is switched off.
The ship has touched sprite X: sets ship_hit and plays sound 5. A double-size sprite takes the shield away; any other sprite is switched off.
The bit mask of each sprite slot, for testing collision_bits.
Column of a gun emplacement that fires shells to the left; it moves with the scenery.
Column of each of the five shells.
The second shell's column.
The third shell's column.
The fourth shell's column.
The fifth shell's column.
Row of each shell; 0 when free.
Column offset of each of the gun's five barrels.
Row of each barrel: 9, 10, 12, 14, 15.
Fires a shell from each of the five barrels that has character $C0 beside it, unless a laser (characters $5A-$62) is in front, which it rubs out instead. Sound 6.
Moves each shell a column left, three characters wide ($DC-$DE), until it reaches column 2.
Frames until the gun fires again: 70.
Set by event 11 while the gun is active.
While the gun is on and not past column 4, fires every 70 frames. Event 11, which starts it, never ran in the code map.
Event 11: sets $75B3 to 1, $75B2 to 24 and $7508 to $22. It never ran in the code map.
The bullet bullet_vs_scenery tests this frame.
One bullet a frame: removes it if it is over scenery (a character $80 or above).
Puts back $FB-$FE and cell_x/cell_y as the main program left them, then returns into irq.
Where irq_chain keeps $FB-$FE.
Returns A = 0 if a laser is within a row and a few columns of the sprite's cell (near_col, near_row); otherwise 1.
Y kept by laser_near.
The rusher's column, handed to laser_near.
The rusher's row, handed to laser_near.
Tests each rusher against the shots (rusher_shot) and lasers: the first one hit is destroyed with sound 2, and the rest wait for the next call.
Column of the rusher being tested.
Row of the rusher being tested.
Next rusher.
The Big Core's column, for core_shots.
The Big Core's row.
Returns A = 0, and rubs the shot out, if a shot is within two rows and four columns of cell_x, cell_y.
X kept by rusher_shot.
Runs laser_near for the rusher.
Colours the Vic Viper flashes through: blue, red, light blue, light red.
While ship_flash runs, flashes the Vic Viper's colour; otherwise sets it to its normal colour (11, dark grey, from stars_on).

The stage's end, once event 12 (event_attack) has set boss_mode and stopped the scroll: counts down, clears the remaining enemies, then builds the Big Core and each frame runs its movement, lasers, timer and hits. When its five walls are gone it scores 500 and the stage is cleared; when its timer (core_time) runs out first, the stage is cleared without the points.
Leftover bytes after boss_phase that nothing reads.
While the shield is up, draws the Vic Viper with shape $82 in place of $80.
How far right of its centre the Big Core reaches on each row near its middle, 13 rows: shots inside it are stopped.

Tests the Big Core against the shots: a shot inside its outline is stopped with a small explosion; one of the first seven shots that strikes its two middle rows counts toward a wall (sound 4), every sixth such hit taking a wall (core_hit). Lasers in the middle count too, every eighth touch taking a wall.
Shots still needed to take the next wall: 6 (8 for lasers).
Low bytes of each stage's character block, eight stages.
High bytes of each stage's character block.

Copies the current stage's 1 KB of characters to $3C00, the top half of the character set at $3800, from the address in stage_charset_lo/hi; then loads the stage's 512 bytes at $8000 and its colour row.
Rubs out a laser that reaches the front of any of the gun's barrels.
Low bytes of each stage's 512-byte block for $8000.
High bytes of the same.
Copies 512 bytes for the current stage from stage_block_lo/hi to $8000, then the stage's colours (load_stage_colours).
Low bytes of each stage's 25 row colours.
High bytes of stage_colours' addresses.
Copies the current stage's 25 colour bytes, one per screen row, to row_colours ($41CB).
Frames left in the current 50 for core_clock.
Called each frame of the boss: every 50 frames takes one from core_time.
Counts down once every 50 frames (core_clock) while the Big Core is on screen; at 0 the core leaves and the stage ends without its points.
Lets the first four shots break blocks (character $96) in the next two cells: the block and the shot both go.
A flag that the routine after it flips each call and stage_setup clears; nothing else reads it.
Set when the ship's falling wreck reaches Y $C8, or by quit_key; play_loop then ends the turn.

While the Vic Viper explodes: switches every other sprite off, lets the wreck drift right half a pixel and fall a pixel a frame through eight shapes and colours, leaving explosions as it goes; once below Y $C8 the turn is over.
Frame counter for death_fall's shapes.
The wreck's shapes as it falls.
The wreck's colours as it falls.
Four frames of the spinning capsule, four characters (32 bytes) each, that spin_capsules copies over characters $78-$7B.
The eight steps of the capsule's spin, each naming one of the four frames.
Counter for capsule_order.
Frames until the capsule turns again: 4.
Every fourth frame copies the next of four four-character frames (32 bytes each, from $7AA9), in the eight-step order of capsule_order, over characters $78-$7B, so the capsules seem to spin.
Twelve bytes nothing reads: three steps of 3 2 1 and one of -3 -2 -1, perhaps an old speed table.

Stage 2's phase-2 interrupt work: the shared work, the aimed balls, the ring firers, $79CA, $6634 and the capsules' colours, then on odd frames the explosions and the ring firers' shots, on even frames the homing and wave enemies and the stars.
Kept 0; boss_phase ends the stage only while it is.
